competition: BetVictor Northern Ireland Open 2026 (WST ranking event), Waterfront Hall, Belfast, 18-25 Oct 2026. All six OLBG matches are Round 2 (last 32), best of 7 frames (first to 4), played Wed 21 Oct 2026.
rating_input: Tournament seeding = official WST world ranking at the seeding cut-off, taken from the official draw (snooker.org draw sheet mirrors the WST draw; order of play confirmed on wst.tv match centre). Seedings are a single consistent vintage for all 12 players. Current official Johnstone's Paint World Rankings (2-year money list, wst.tv) captured for cross-check: Higgins 6 (£905,000), Bingham 19 (£350,550), Slessor 23 (£329,200), J. Jones 24 (£319,300), Pang Junxu 29 (£272,750); the WST page only server-renders the top 36, so seedings are used as the uniform model input.
model: Strength from seeding: frame win probability for the higher-ranked (lower number) player = 1/(1+exp(-0.40 x (ln(rank_worse) - ln(rank_better)))). Independent frames, first to 4. Markets originated: Win Match, frame Handicap (-1.5 / -2.5 frames on the favourite), total frames over/under 5.5, and most likely correct scores (Frame Betting). No century-breaks or high-break markets (no verified break-building inputs collected).
event_flag: Round 1 produced an exceptional run of upsets (world No.1 seed casualties included Trump, O’Sullivan, Murphy, Selby, Robertson, Zhao, Xiao, Hawkins, Wakelin) - best-of-7 variance is high; confidence tiers still follow the mechanical model, but this is flagged in Findings.

matches.form_context: Cheung Ka Wai (world No.106 seed) beat Ronnie O’Sullivan 4-3 in round 1 - the win of his career. Bingham (2015 world champion, current official No.19, £350,550) beat Yao Pengcheng 4-2 in round 1.
Liam Davies (No.89 seed) knocked out Shaun Murphy (No.8 seed) 4-2 in round 1. Pang Junxu beat Alfie Burden 4-2 in round 1.
Jamie Jones (No.60 seed) beat Chris Wakelin (No.13 seed) 4-1 in round 1. Slessor received a walkover (He Guoqiang withdrew for medical reasons), so plays his first match of the event here.

Martin O'Donnell (world No.55/56) beat Judd Trump 4-3 on Monday night with breaks of 64, 50 and 52, leading by a frame three times. Brecel (2023 world champion, now seeded 39) beat Lei Peifan 4-1 in round 1.
Higgins (official world No.6, £905,000) beat Liam Highfield 4-1 with a 121 break - the first top-16 player to win on table one this week. Jak Jones beat Tom Ford 4-1 in round 1.
Both won as underdogs in round 1: Sam Craigie (No.70 seed) edged Xiao Guodong (No.12 seed) 4-3; Rickie Walden whitewashed Ali Carter (No.23 seed) 4-0.
